title: Sound -> light for concerts/festivals, TRAINED ON DANCE datasets (LightSem v2): generative audio -> light on dance-derived targets
description: Accepted representation-first implementation 2026-09-10. Build convincing music-driven stage lighting. Music is the only playback input; an internal generated skeleton/motion sequence is explicitly allowed. Hybrid measured audio dynamics may control brightness and movement intensity. Quiet passages must remain visible but restrained. Establish clean motion-source and temporal-codec quality before audio training. Prior human review rejects flashing/juggling reconstructions and excessive Shpongle movement; only the incumbent audio-to-descriptions-to-pose path is currently visually convincing. Glare improvement is useful but does not establish visible head-brightness dynamics. Exploration seed0; confirm only qualifying finalist and matched baseline at seed1. Accelerated BF16/compile/prefetch in matched arms, no earlier 2–3h ceiling. Historical nulls and gates remain valid.

updates.text: 2026-09-03 rev. 2 (Anton's correction): dance datasets are the TRAINING SET for a sound->light model; no music-to-dance generation at inference. Rev. 1's 'latent dancer' inference path is withdrawn; generators survive only as an optional offline pseudo-labelling teacher (PLAN.md section 8). Runbooks rb-ls2-00..05 rewritten accordingly.

2026-09-04 rev. 3: integrated four Perplexity reasoning passes (audio->light design; music-induced-movement science; causal model + latency; dataset audit degenerated, replaced by direct source checks) and Anton's note on extracting motion from video with pose models. Targets split into deterministic skeleton / event point-process / sampled style residual; rig mapping follows the body; two-path deployment (transients on a 10-20 ms DSP path) because ITU-R BT.1359-1 detectability is +45 ms when sound leads. New runbooks 00b (predictability audit) and 00c (late-lights + category-error tests) run BEFORE any training.

2026-09-04 Stage 0b resolved in two halves (exp-002, exp-003). AIST++ cannot supply block A: genre explains 0.65-0.96 of between-track movement variance and Burger 2013 does not replicate, several correlations invert. Free dancing to EDM can: held-out-track R2 +0.30 for the shared movement curve on Oslo, drop/breakdown ratio 1.7-2.5x with Cohen's d up to 2.55. The binding constraint moves from 'is there a signal' to 'how much free-dance data can we get'.

2026-09-04 implementation pass complete (exp-004..exp-008): descriptor extractor (mocap and video), constant-tempo beat grid, canonical-rig conductors, evaluation suite with nulls, 9.3 M causal Conformer with three heads, streaming inference, blind A/B harness; 14 of 14 verification checks. Stage 1 light gates fail (+0.017 vs real-mapped +0.216); operator head passes (+0.31 lift, z 3.66); latency budget met.

2026-09-04 repair pass (exp-009): the Stage 1 audio bus read up to 375 ms of the future through librosa defaults; fixed, retrained, held-out block A R2 +0.0438 -> +0.0192, which is the size of the artefact. Event-rate calibration did not raise Light-BAS (predicted mechanism wrong). The surplus light events come from the sampled channels' 11-452x corpus HF energy. Product pivoted to the offline pre-rendered path (rb-ls2-07, PLAN rev. 6).

2026-09-04 Stage 0c category test (exp-010): dance-derived hybrid light beats the beat trigger 8-1 (1 equal) on 'looks like a lighting engineer', ties 5-4 on 'on the music'; one rater, 10 brightness-matched AIST++ pairs. Category error rejected directionally; block C stays. Rater's tell for 'not an engineer' was change rate, the same defect the model carries.

2026-09-04 Stage 8 queued (rb-ls2-08): 338 Just Dance gameplay captures (22.0 h, full songs, one filmed stylised coach or several -- each coach its own channel; research-only). Three signals: coach motion for block A/C, hand-animated background lighting as a designed show for HEAD B, full-song structure for H-C. Decision measurement is the held-out-song predictability audit. Extraction launched 15:00 with YOLO26m-pose at 960 after a six-clip trial (solos and multi-coach at >= 0.998 coverage per coach).

2026-09-04 Stage 7 (rb-ls2-07), three of four hypotheses tested. H-A (exp-012): the look-ahead ceiling fails both gates -- with the whole track visible, held-out block A R2 on AIST++ is -0.009 against the causal +0.019 and the light gates do not move; the corpus binds, not the model. H-B (exp-011): spectral matching is the largest lever found -- a causal one-pole per channel fitted to the corpus above-6 Hz energy takes model Light-BAS from +0.018 to +0.293 (real-mapped +0.211), FID 67 -> 20, light events 86 -> 35 per clip against 30 real, diversity not falling; the 12 Hz filter the hypothesis named does nothing, the mismatch sits near 0.2 Hz; zero-phase at matched cutoffs scores the same, so the offline path removes lag, not jitter. H-D (exp-013): audio alone does not anticipate an operator's scene change 4 s ahead (offline margin -0.02, CI spanning zero); a 10x first result was a leak through target-derived hazard features under a symmetric window, caught by the shift control. H-C waits for the Just Dance corpus.

2026-09-04 (evening) Stage 9 queued (rb-ls2-09-designed-light, PLAN.md rev. 8 section 6.9). Anton's reading of the shipped Just Dance model: decent, not human. Five outside passes with the full brief (Perplexity deep research x1, reasoning x4: audio decomposition, datasets in two halves, multimodal methods, mixture of light) plus Skip-BART (arXiv:2506.01482) and SeqLight (arXiv:2605.03660) read in full agree on the diagnosis: the bottleneck is the target (dance is a weak proxy; coaches agree at r 0.22-0.42), the hand-written conductor, and the absence of human preference -- not the trunk, causality or the amount of dance. Deep-research verdict: 'another music-to-motion transformer will not close the gap; the project needs authored lighting intent, a learned hierarchical planner, and a preference model that tells deliberate composition from synchronised motion'. Datasets: no public, commercially clean corpus of professional DMX programming exists; RPMC-L2 (all 699 now cached, CC-BY-4.0, no waveform) is the only public stage-domain set; authored light exists at scale in xLights free .xsq sequences (~556, ~25-40 h, audio not included) and Beat Saber lightshow maps (v3 group event boxes with phase-spread filters, verified on the API); console show files only by contract. Seven hypotheses queued: H-G stems (audit-gated), H-H corpus predictability gate, H-I group-effects decoder (the mixture of light, SeqLight's split), H-J section planner on the knobs, H-K factorised critic with beat-trigger negatives as best-of-N, H-L Bradley-Terry knobs from 200-400 pairs, H-M frozen encoder vs random projection. Rule-outs added: AR light LM decoder, RL on the flow head before the critic gate, type-MoE in the trunk, section/chord/LRA/timbre bus channels, Jukebox/CLAP, fixture-token decoder before console data, product training on research corpora.

2026-09-05: Stage 9 (rb-ls2-09) run end to end; H-H, H-G, H-M, H-J, H-K directional-only, H-I refuted as built, H-L open (exp-017..023). Reading: the authored corpora on disk (RPMC-L2, Just Dance visual, Beat Saber) support learning WHEN a look changes and the corpus's look statistics, not per-frame or per-bar light levels; the decent-not-human gap is not closed by stems, a frozen encoder, a regressed or sampled group decoder, a bar planner or a critic reranker. Engine diagnostic: with the phase spread zeroed the v1 decoder's Light-BAS minus null is +0.51 (conductor +0.13) at fewer events than the conductor, so the BAS miss was the engine; FID_light and the missing human test carry the verdict. Next: cue-based rendering from the calibrated look-change hazard, scored on cue timing and look-transition statistics; the H-L human preference study; console show files for level design.

2026-09-10 explicit user authorization: implement the accepted representation-first plan. This supersedes prior no-internal-motion restrictions. Previous description preserved:
Binding product objective, clarified by Anton on2026-09-08: lights and moving fixtures should dance to music using a model trained on measured dancer motion. Inference takes music only; no dancer or pose input is required. Whole-song context is allowed. No algorithmic beat/downbeat/bar grid, BPM metronome, preset pulse/chase/strobe, travelling wave, sinusoidal aiming or hue-drift generator may supply the choreography. Fixture translation may convert learned controls into geometry/DMX and enforce physical ranges/speed limits without inventing temporal patterns. With fixed learned controls, light should settle to a fixed state.

The current Stage11 scene path does not meet this objective. It predicts six scene-colour statistics and then applies fixed beat pulses/waves. The Shpongle demonstration used a90BPM uniform grid (0.666667s intervals); Anton observed repetitive flashing. The separate learned-descriptor aiming prototype removed the pan/tilt pendulum only. The historical motion model also includes beat-derived input features and a music-relative metric_level target; masking inputs only at inference would not constitute a validated beat-free trained model.

Stage11's limited positive findings remain: temporal scene dynamics and audio-conditioning controls passed independently audited validation and locked-test gates (H11-T/A supports), but expanded-data motion improvement failed validation (H11-D directional_only). This is not an end-to-end aesthetic or dance-transfer win. The39-rating H-L pilot remains unconfirmed and new48-pair materials are unrated. Historical Stage9/10 recipe failures and their scope remain preserved. The immediate architecture requirement and limitations are recorded in /root/lightsem/docs/DANCE_DRIVEN_CONTRACT.md and /root/lightsem/docs/STAGE11_RESULTS_20260908.md. synthesis:
STATE OF KNOWLEDGE — 2026-09-08, continuation audit + incremental primary-source literature review.

Scope: pre-rendered audio -> stage lighting; whole-song context allowed; dance is training supervision only. The old causal-only/no-experiments synthesis is superseded. Current learned renderer uses the descriptor/event/style model with ConductorHybrid. Stage9 GroupEngine and generic CLI are separate entry points.

Local evidence: repeated tuning of stems, frozen audio features, model size, per-bar level regression, six-moment group decoding and critic/cue recipes did not close the designed-appearance gap. Strong synchronization scores can coexist with poor aesthetics. Historical supports/directional-only records are not blanket product gates. GroupDecoder is not a faithful Skip-BART/SeqLight implementation: it omits autoregressive light tokens, histogram targets and learned temporal decomposition. Existing recurrence analysis retains boundaries but not motif memory. Per-bar regression therefore does not rule out explicit motif reuse.

Human pilot:39ratings, one rater,29registered song groups. Held-out preference-model accuracy56.4%/59.0% with intervals including chance; music accuracy equals its majority-side baseline and appearance logloss0.739 is worse than0.693 chance. Fresh generated-candidate-vs-default wins are unmeasured. These ratings do not test new GroupEngine wave/colour controls. Median screen-luma mismatch16.1%; the blinder metric squares dimmer while the renderer is linear. Preserve old data/scores, version the correction, verify canonical audio identity and material matching before fresh preference claims.

New literature adds implementable SLS/EUBO preference acquisition, editable light-object layers (Glow with the Flow), explicit hierarchical/repetition representations, Beat This timing models and Raveform annotation access. Transfer to LightSem is untested. Glow with the Flow itself reports that synchronization/congruence ratings miss repetition and colour-richness defects. SeqLight weight release is not verified. RPMC is video-derived colour supervision, not professional DMX logs; no newly usable authored-control corpus was established.

Next experiments, in order of dependencies: material/metric validation; isolated beat benchmark; explicit recurrence-memory vs equally varied no-memory composition; active vs random pair acquisition; histogram/assignment oracle followed only conditionally by matched audio-conditioned training; independently reviewed authored-look oracle to measure renderer/planner capability. Budgets and thresholds in the report are proposals, not preregistrations. Confirm primary outcomes, independence unit and gates before execution; do not interpret an oracle failure as a uniquely identified cause.

No new training/rendering/GPU job or experiment closure was performed in this review. Additional Just Dance extraction remains a separate process; freeze and audit completed features before using new data. Existing interpretation debt and statuses are not cleared by this synthesis.
